BILL NUMBER:  S2962

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to olive
oil products


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to ensure that olive oil sold in the State
meets certain quality and labeling standards.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
The bill would require the Department of Agriculture and Markets to
promulgate rules and regulations for the production and labeling of
olive oil. The bill stipulates that such regulations shall
substantially comply with the standards of the prevailing
international voluntary consensus olive oil trade organization (the
International Olive Oil Council), or the standards for olive oil as
adopted by the US Food and Drug Administration when such standards
have been adopted. A manufacturer that fails to meet the standards
promulgated would be subject to enforcement by the Department for
selling a misbranded product. The bill would also prohibit additives
in virgin olive oils and restrict the concentration of
alpha-tocopherol in olive oil products to an amount not to exceed
220mg/kg.

 JUSTIFICATION :
U.S. standards for olive oil have not been updated since the late
1940's which makes it easy for some manufacturers and suppliers to cut
corners and quality. Connecticut and California have already passed
similar laws and the North American Olive Oil Association supports the
legislation.

In 2007, on two separate occasions, US Marshals along with FDA
investigators and New York District Investigators seized oil
misbranded and being sold as extra virgin olive oil and pomace olive
oil at a total estimated retail value of $705,000.00. The misbranded
oil was actually soybean oil which is significantly less expensive
than olive oil.

Lax food production and labeling standards can present a safety
hazard, especially to those with food allergies. An estimated 12
million people, including 3 million children suffer from food
allergies.  People with the most common food allergies such as soy,
peanuts, tree nuts, eggs, milk, wheat, fish and shellfish, or any food
allergy, should know if their virgin olive oil is pure.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall become a law. Effective immediately the Commissioner of
Agriculture and Markets is authorized to promulgate any rules or
regulations necessary for the implementation of this act on its
effective date.

 TITLE OF BILL :

in virgin olive oils and restrict the concentration of
alpha-tocopherol in olive oil products to an amount not to exceed
220mg/kg.

U.S. standards for olive oil have not been updated since the late
1940's which makes it easy for some manufacturers and suppliers to cut
comers and quality. Connecticut and California have already passed
similar laws and the North American Olive Oil Association supports the
legislation.

In 2007, on two separate occasions, US Marshals along with FDA
investigators and New York District Investigators seized oil
misbranded and being sold as extra virgin olive oil and pomace olive
oil at a total estimated retail value of $705,000.00. The misbranded
oil was actually soybean oil which is significantly less expensive
than olive oil.

Lax food production and labeling standards can present a safety
hazard, especially to those with food allergies. An estimated 12
million people, including 3 million children suffer from food
allergies.  People with the most common food allergies such as soy,
peanuts, tree nuts, eggs, milk, wheat, fish and shellfish, or any food
allergy, should know if their virgin olive oil is pure.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall become a law. Effective immediately the Commissioner of
Agriculture and Markets is authorized to promulgate any rules or
regulations necessary for the implementation of this act on its
effective date.

summary: Relates to the labeling of oil olive; provides that the commissioner of agriculture and market shall develop standards for the labeling of olive oil, olive-pomace oil, refined olive oil and virgin olive oil which conform to national or other recognized standards.
title: Relates to standards and the labeling of olive oils
